newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan finalises bills on revising BOJ law - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan finalises bills on revising BOJ law - MOF.

text.p: The government on Monday finalised bills to revise the decades-old Bank of Japan Law with the aim of increasing the independence of the central bank, the Finance Ministry said.
The legislation is expected to be approved at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday and will then be sent to the current parliamentary session.
The revision is almost in line with a set of proposals which a government advisory panel announced last December.
The plan, which aims to free the central bank from the grip of the powerful Finance Ministry, is part of the deregulation plans promoted by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
The revision is aimed at strengthening the independence of the BOJ in setting monetary policy by limiting intervention by the Finance Ministry into the BOJ's decisions.
Currently, the government can order the BOJ to postpone monetary policy decisions should the central bank's views differ from those of the government.

Under the new legislation, the government can still directly intervene in BOJ policy decisions by asking the BOJ policy-making board to delay monetary policy decisions, though the board will have the ultimate say in whether to carry them out.
The revision will obligate the BOJ to testify about its monetary policies before parliament whenever required by parliament.
The BOJ will be also obligated to submit to parliament a report on its decisions on monetary policy about every six months.
The BOJ governor and the deputy governor will serve terms of five years, unchanged from the current law.
